subject: SLA Exception: scheduled nightly ETL window — temporary rate-band uplift request
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@novushealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@novushealth.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Request: temporary nightly rate-band uplift for ETL window

Hi Kimberly,

We're doing a migration next week that consolidates several data streams. The nightly ETL window (02:00–05:00 PST) on Jan 20–26 will see sustained high-throughput API calls to Redwood. Under the current rate band we're seeing repeated throttling and elevated tail latency in staging; if that happens in prod we'll have failed jobs and missed downstream SLAs.

Can Redwood grant a temporary rate-band uplift (roughly 3x current per-minute token limit) for that window and commit to preserving latency targets (p95 < 180ms for generation calls) for the duration? Novus is prepared to sign a short addendum.

We're attaching the job schedule and an estimated RPS/Tokens profile. Can you confirm feasibility and any guardrails you need (monitoring, rollback triggers)?

Thanks,
Daniel Park
SRE Lead — NovusHealth

Attachments: etl-schedule.csv (text/csv)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: temporary nightly rate-band uplift for ETL window

Thanks Daniel — and sorry to hear staging showed problems. I'm looping in Markus (runtime) and Laura (SLA/ops) to scope options. Quick asks from our side so we can size the uplift:

- peak tokens/minute and 95th percentile tokens/minute for the peak hour
- expected concurrency (approx RPS) per job type during window
- whether requests are predominantly short generations (<=256 tokens) or long-running streams

Markus — can you outline feasible mitigations (temporary fairness override, reserved token pool, or dedicated route) and what telemetry/rollback hooks we'd require?

Daniel — if you can drop the CSV and approximate numbers into the Drive link (you already attached the schedule — thanks), we'll draft a short addendum for signature.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 08:23:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary nightly rate-band uplift for ETL window

Kimberly, Laura — technical summary and recommendation below.

Observations (staging): increased token bursts have caused our fairness policy to throttle Novus bots intermittently; tail latency spikes when KV-cache misses are frequent.

Options:
1) Short-term fairness override for a 3-night window (02:00–05:00 PST) that increases per-customer token ceiling by 3x. Fastest to implement but needs strict rollback triggers and token caps per-minute to avoid noisy neighbors.
2) Temporary dedicated route onto a small reserved pool (preferred if Novus can tolerate a slight provisioning lead time). Preserves tenant isolation and predictable latency; costs are higher.
3) On-the-fly quantization/packing suggestions (helpful but incremental).

Proposal: implement option #1 with these guardrails:
- Automated monitoring: p99 latency > 300ms or error rate > 0.5% triggers immediate rollback.
- Runbook: enable at 01:30 PST, smoke-checks until 03:30, rollback window 01:30–06:00 if triggers hit.
- SLA addendum (attached) that notes uplift dates and rollback criteria; Novus signs before we enable.

Attaching early draft: sla-addendum-draft.pdf

Markus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
